sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Recall the Chain Rule: d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Visualize a function as y = f(x) (Explicit). Introduce the concept of a relation where y is 'trapped' inside an equation, like a squirrel hiding inside a hollow tree.
sections.example: Explicit: y = x^2. Implicit: x^2 + y^2 = 25 (The Circle).

sections.title: The Core Logic: The 'y-is-a-function' Rule
sections.content: Treat 'y' as a function of x, y(x). Whenever you differentiate a term with 'y', you must multiply by dy/dx due to the Chain Rule. Use a visual 'dy/dx alert' icon whenever y is differentiated.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Procedure: The Robotic Workflow
sections.content: 1. Differentiate both sides with respect to x. 2. Apply Chain Rule to 'y' terms. 3. Collect all dy/dx terms on one side. 4. Factor out dy/dx and solve.
sections.example: Find dy/dx for x^2 + y^2 = 25. Step 1: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Step 2: dy/dx = -2x / 2y = -x/y.

sections.title: Visual Application: The Tangent of a Robot Arm
sections.content: Visualize a robotic arm moving along a non-function curve (e.g., a Folium of Descartes). We need the slope (dy/dx) to adjust the robot's orientation at a specific point. The graphical tangent line 'snaps' to the curve automatically.
sections.example: Point (2, 2) on the curve x^3 + y^3 = 9xy. Apply the method to find the slope of the robot's path at that coordinate.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Recap: Implicit differentiation is just the Chain Rule applied to equations. Remind students that the result dy/dx may contain both x and y. A quick checklist for common pitfalls: Did you forget the dy/dx on the y-term?
sections.example: Check: Always substitute the point (x, y) into your final dy/dx expression to find the numerical slope.
